newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S CELLPHONE COURT SAGA TAKES NEW TWIST.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S CELLPHONE COURT SAGA TAKES NEW TWIST.

text.p: The complicated legal saga surrounding the Brazilian government's B Band cellular telephone sale program took another twist Tuesday when four consortia asked a high court to disqualify a recent concession-winner.

The consortia asked the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ) to quash an injunction that allowed the Tess group to take part in the B Band program and win the Sao Paulo state concession, an STJ spokesman said.

Tess, which includes Swedish telecom firm Telia, was originally disqualified from the B Band program in June by a Communications Ministry committee for failing to use a Brazil-based translator in its initial application.
The group then won its injunction from the STJ allowing it to take part in the program.
Tess came first in Friday's bidding for the Sao Paulo concession, which does not include the city of Sao Paulo, when it offered $1.0 billion for the license.

Should Tess be disqualified -- either as a result of Tuesday's case brought by the four rival consortia, or in a final ruling on the merit of its appeal to take part in the B Band program -- the Sao Paulo state contract would be awarded to the Avantel group, placed second in the bidding.
Avantel comprises Brazilian construction companies Odebrecht and Camargo Correa, Unibanco bank and AirTouch Communications of the United States.
There was yet a further possible winner of the concession.

The Telet group, which includes BCE Inc's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc, last week won an injunction allowing its bid for the Sao Paulo state concession to remain unopened, pending an appeal on its disqualification from the B Band program.
That appeal was due to be ruled upon Wednesday in the STJ.
